bull.b: Recurring revenue growth and 169 fully validated systems show the installed base is converting into ongoing consumables and service demand. This model can compound beyond individual instrument sales as utilization rises, improving revenue visibility and making commercial progress more durable over the next several quarters.

Gross margin improved to a record 15% from 4% year over year, while service margin reached 49%. The improvement indicates operating execution and mix benefits are emerging; if sustained, higher service profitability can support broader margin expansion as the installed base grows.

Consumables growth above 20% and nine Q2 validations versus two a year earlier indicate stronger adoption and workflow conversion. More validated systems and routine testing should expand recurring consumable pull-through, supporting the company’s stated growth ambitions beyond one-time placements.

bear.b: Q2 net loss of $12.9 million and adjusted EBITDA loss of $10.3 million show that improved revenue and gross margin have not yet translated into operating profitability. Continued large losses limit internally funded growth and leave the business dependent on execution and external capital over the medium term.

bear.t: Negative cash generation and funding dependence
bear.b: Operating and free cash flow have remained negative across all periods, with Q2 cash usage described as higher than normal. A roughly $20 million cash balance and reliance on debt milestones or warrant proceeds make funding continuity sensitive to operating performance and financing execution.

bear.t: Negative product margin and high operating expense
bear.b: Q2 product margin remained negative 3% despite improvement, while full-year operating expense guidance is $51–$53 million. The core system economics therefore remain below breakeven and substantial spending continues, delaying scalable profitability until pricing, mix, or cost efficiency improves.
